name: Advanced Authorization Patterns
description: This module describes advanced patterns for authorization intended for non-trivial cases where the basic approach is insufficient.
content:
This module describes advanced patterns for authorization intended for non-trivial cases where the basic approach is insufficient.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. When authorization decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
2. Re-check edge cases relevant to authorization (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
3. Check that authorization terminology is used consistently throughout, matching existing conventions in the surrounding context.
4. Keep authorization changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
5. Surface known limitations of a chosen authorization approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
6. Prefer the simplest authorization approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
7. Document any non-obvious authorization decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not silently drop authorization edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.
- Avoid introducing new authorization abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.
- Avoid mixing unrelated authorization concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.
- Do not skip documenting authorization assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of authorization correctness.

CLOSING NOTE
Revisit these authorization guidelines if the task's constraints change significantly during the work.
